text: AMFI Mutual Fund Tax Implications Guide Taxation on equity mutual funds in India: Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) tax is 20% if equity units are redeemed within 12 months of allotment. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax is 12.5% on gains exceeding ₹1.25 Lakh per financial year if equity units are redeemed after 12 months.

AMFI Scheme Benchmark Guidelines As per AMFI/SEBI guidelines, every mutual fund scheme must compare its performance against a target index known as the benchmark. HDFC Top 100 Large Cap Fund is benchmarked against the NIFTY 100 TRI. HDFC Mid-Cap Opportunities Fund is benchmarked against NIFTY Midcap 150 TRI. HDFC Flexi Cap, Focused 30, and ELSS Tax Saver are benchmarked against NIFTY 500 TRI.

AMFI ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) Guide Equity Linked Savings Scheme (ELSS) is a category of mutual funds that offers tax savings under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act. Under AMFI guidelines, ELSS funds have a mandatory lock-in period of 3 years from the date of allotment. Redemptions, switches, or withdrawals are not permitted before the completion of 3 years.

HDFC Mutual Fund exit load, expense ratio, and other fees HDFC Mutual Fund charge structures: HDFC Mid-Cap, Flexi Cap, Focused 30, and Top 100 charge an exit load of 1% if redeemed or switched out within 1 year (365 days) from the date of allotment. No exit load is charged if redeemed after 1 year. The HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund has Nil exit load. However, the ELSS fund has a mandatory lock-in period of 3 years. The Expense Ratio represents the management and operational fees charged by HDFC Asset Management Company for managing the funds, which ranges between 0.70% and 0.80% for direct plans.

AMFI Riskometer Guidelines The Riskometer is an educational tool introduced by SEBI/AMFI that visually represents the risk level of mutual fund schemes. It has 6 risk levels: Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High, and Very High risk. All five HDFC equity schemes (Mid-Cap Opportunities, Flexi Cap, Focused 30, ELSS Tax Saver, and Top 100) are categorized in the 'Very High Risk' level, denoting high equity exposure.

HDFC Mutual Fund Scheme FAQs Find answers to general questions about HDFC Mutual Fund schemes. You can query specific metrics such as NAV, AUM, Expense Ratio, and exit loads. All HDFC Mutual Fund equity schemes offer Direct and Regular plans. Factual details are updated regularly from the scheme information documents.

SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations and FAQs The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates mutual funds to protect investors. SEBI guidelines state that all information regarding mutual fund fees, riskometer, benchmark, and exit load must be disclosed transparently. SEBI strictly prohibits distributors or assistants from providing investment recommendations or advice without a SEBI Investment Adviser (RIA) registration.

How to Download HDFC Mutual Fund Account Statement To download your HDFC Mutual Fund Account Statement: 1. Go to the HDFC MF Portal (www.hdfcfund.com) or use the 'HDFC MF Online' mobile app. 2. Log in using your PAN, Folio Number, or Username. 3. Navigate to 'Statements' -> 'Account Statement'. 4. Select the Folio, Scheme, and Date Range, then click 'Download PDF' or choose 'Email Me' to get the statement on your registered email address.

How to Download HDFC Capital Gains Statement To download your HDFC Capital Gains Statement for tax filing: 1. Log in to the HDFC Mutual Fund official portal. 2. Navigate to the 'Statements' or 'Service Requests' section. 3. Click on 'Capital Gains Statement'. 4. Select the relevant Financial Year, Folio Number, and click 'Download PDF' or 'Email Statement' to get your transaction tax report.
